scene: 会议室里，有人把一份厚厚的改革方案摊开，主张从制度本身动手。The committee proposed radical changes to the way the city collects waste.
sceneCN: 这里 radical 是「根本的、彻底的」（第 1 个义项：触及事物根基因而彻底的）；句意为委员会提议对城市收运垃圾的方式进行彻底改革。画面里可留意：摊开的厚方案、被翻到卷边的页角。

pos.zh: 根本的；彻底的；激进的；根生的
激进分子；（数学）根式；（语言）词根

derivatives.zh: radical 加 -ly，指从根本上、彻底地
radical 加 -ism，指主张彻底变革的激进主义
radical 加 -ize，指使某人变得激进

senses.title: Relating to the root of a matter
senses.definition: touching the root or foundation of a problem, and therefore thorough
senses.definitionCN: 触及问题的根源或基础，因而十分彻底
senses.example: The plan calls for radical changes in the tax system.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划要求对税制进行彻底改革。
senses.why: Latin radix meant a root, and radicalis meant belonging to a root, so a radical change goes down to the root of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 radix 意为根，radicalis 意为属于根的，因此 radical change 就是深入到事物根部的改变。

senses.title: Wanting great political change
senses.definition: favouring far-reaching change in politics or society, often by rapid means
senses.definitionCN: 主张在政治或社会上进行影响深远的改变，常指以较快手段实现
senses.example: The party's radical wing wants to abolish the old rules.
senses.exampleCN: 该党的激进派想废除旧规则。
senses.why: A reformer who wants to reach the root of a social problem is called radical, because the root is exactly what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 想触及社会问题根源的改革者被称为 radical，因为这个词命名的正是「根」。

senses.title: A person who wants such change
senses.definition: someone who holds radical political views and works for them
senses.definitionCN: 持激进政治观点并为之行动的人
senses.example: He was a radical in his youth and a moderate later.
senses.exampleCN: 他年轻时是激进分子，后来成了温和派。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the person who carries the quality, a common path in English.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，用来指具有这种性质的人，这是英语里常见的路径。

senses.title: Growing from the root
senses.definition: growing from or near the root of a plant, as some leaves do
senses.definitionCN: 从植物根部或近根部生长，如某些叶子
senses.example: Radical leaves of this plant lie almost flat on the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的根生叶几乎平贴在地面上。
senses.why: Botany kept the plain Latin sense: a part attached at the root is literally radical.
senses.whyCN: 植物学保留了拉丁语最朴素的意思：附着在根部的部分字面上就是 radical。

senses.title: A root expression in mathematics
senses.definition: a mathematical expression written with a root sign, or the sign itself
senses.definitionCN: 用根号写成的数学表达式，或根号本身
senses.example: Simplify the radical before you add the two terms.
senses.exampleCN: 先把根式化简，再把两项相加。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the root image directly: the radical sign points to the root of a number.
senses.whyCN: 数学直接使用「根」这一意象：根号所指的就是一个数的根。

intro.en: Radical comes from the Latin word for root and its adjective, and the sense of thoroughness grew from the picture of reaching down to the root.
intro.cn: radical 源自拉丁语表示根的名词及其形容词，而「彻底」这一层意思从「向下触及根部」的画面生长出来。

items.en: Radix meant the root of a plant and, figuratively, the base or origin of anything.
items.cn: radix 指植物的根，也比喻任何事物的基础或起源。

items.en: The genitive radicis, of a root, supplied the stem from which the adjective was formed.
items.cn: 属格 radicis（根的）提供了构成形容词的词干。

items.en: Radicalis meant belonging to a root, and it was used in grammar and medicine as well as in botany.
items.cn: radicalis 意为属于根的，除植物学外也用于语法与医学。

items.en: English took the word for what goes to the root of a matter, and politics gave it the sense of far-reaching change.
items.cn: 英语接受这个词，用来指触及事物根本的东西，政治又赋予它「影响深远之变革」的意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps the senses of root cause, political extreme, root growth and the root sign in algebra.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了根本原因、政治上的极端、根部生长，以及代数中的根号这几层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of depth and extremes.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「根」词干上的词；近义组收表示深入与极端的形容词。

entries.definition: A small red root vegetable eaten raw.
entries.definitionCN: 一种生食的小红根菜。

entries.definition: To remove something completely, as if by pulling it out by the root.
entries.definitionCN: 像连根拔起那样彻底清除某物。

entries.definition: In a thorough or fundamental way.
entries.definitionCN: 以彻底或根本的方式。

entries.definition: The belief in far-reaching change.
entries.definitionCN: 主张彻底变革的信念。

entries.definition: Forming the base of something.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某物基础的。

entries.definition: Extreme and severe in effect.
entries.definitionCN: 作用极端而严厉的。

entries.definition: Far beyond the ordinary.
entries.definitionCN: 远远超出寻常的。

entries.definition: Complete in every detail.
entries.definitionCN: 每个细节都完备的。

normalIntro.en: The root is the picture: a change that goes to the root, a plant part at the root, and the root sign in algebra.
normalIntro.cn: 「根」就是这幅画面的核心：深入根部的改变、长在根部的植物部分，以及代数里的根号。

normal.en: Radical, radish and eradicate all share the Latin word for root, which makes the family easy to hold together.
normal.cn: radical、radish 与 eradicate 都共用拉丁语「根」一词，整族词因此很容易串在一起。

normal.en: A radical reform is not just a big reform; it is one that reaches the root of the system.
normal.cn: radical reform 不只是大改革，而是触及制度根基的改革。

normal.en: The radical sign in mathematics is shaped like a roof over a number, pointing back to its root.
normal.cn: 数学里的根号形状像一个盖在数字上的屋顶，指向它的根。

normal.en: Radical leaves grow at the base of the plant, which is the literal botanical sense.
normal.cn: radical leaves 长在植物基部，这正是植物学里的字面义。

normal.en: Radicalism is the noun for the belief, radicalize the verb for making someone hold it.
normal.cn: radicalism 是表示这种主张的名词，radicalize 是使某人接受它的动词。

abstract.en: To change something radically is to admit that the visible problem was only a symptom.
abstract.cn: 彻底改变某物，就是承认看得见的问题只是症状。

abstract.en: The same word can mean wise depth or dangerous haste, depending on who is describing the change.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可指有智慧的深刻，也可指危险的急躁，取决于谁在描述这场改变。

abstract.en: Everything grows from a root, so the word for root quietly honors what is usually invisible.
abstract.cn: 万物都从根部长出，因此「根」这个词也在悄悄致敬那些通常看不见的部分。

examples.en: The company needs radical changes, not small adjustments.
examples.cn: 这家公司需要彻底变革，而不是小修小补。

examples.en: His radical views made him unpopular with the board.
examples.cn: 他的激进观点使他不受董事会欢迎。

examples.en: In algebra, we first simplify the radical and then solve the equation.
examples.cn: 在代数里，我们先化简根式，再解方程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐的抠」——锐利地往根里抠，一直挖到最根本处，记住 radical 是根本的、激进的。

root: 拉丁语 radix（根）→ radicis（根的）→ 晚期拉丁语 radicalis（属于根的）→ 英语 radical；同族有 radish、eradicate、radically。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a root; the senses divide into a root-deep change, a political extreme, the person holding it, growth at the root and the root sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「根」；义项分为深入根源的改变、政治上的极端、持此立场的人、根部的生长，以及根号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree pulled up by its roots, earth still clinging to them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵被连根拔起的树，根须上还挂着泥土。

branches.en: a knife cutting down to the base
branches.cn: 一直切到根基的一刀

branches.en: a speaker demanding a new order
branches.cn: 要求建立新秩序的发言者

branches.en: leaves lying flat at the stem base
branches.cn: 平贴茎基部的叶子

branches.en: a sign drawn over a number
branches.cn: 画在数字上方的符号

branches.en: the same depth, once in a repair and once in politics
branches.cn: 同一种深入，一次在修补中，一次在政治中

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin noun for root, its stem and adjective ending, with English endings for adverbs, beliefs and verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示根的名词、其词干与形容词词尾构成，再加上表示副词、主张与动词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem radic- is short but reaches English in several common words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 radic- 很短，却在英语里伸进了好几个常用词。

definition_zh: 收音机；广播；无线电；用无线电发送
definition_en: a device that receives broadcast sound; the broadcasting of sound by radio waves; the technology of sending signals by electromagnetic waves; to send a message by radio
core_image: 一台老式收音机的指针停在刻度盘上，扬声器微微发亮
scene: 厨房里，老式收音机的指针在刻度上滑动，水壶的蒸汽把窗玻璃蒙上一层白雾。She turned the radio down when the phone rang.
sceneCN: 这里 radio 是「收音机」（第 1 个义项：接收广播声音的装置）；句意为电话响时她把收音机的声音调小了。画面里可留意：刻度盘上的指针、冒汽的水壶、蒙雾的窗。

pos.zh: 收音机；广播；无线电
用无线电发送；用无线电联络

derivatives.zh: radio 与 man 复合，指从事无线电通信工作的人
radio 与 controlled 复合，指靠无线电操纵的
radio- 与 isotope 复合，指具有放射性的同位素

senses.title: A receiving device
senses.definition: a piece of equipment that picks up broadcast sound and plays it
senses.definitionCN: 接收广播声音并播放出来的设备
senses.example: She turned on the radio in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她在厨房里打开了收音机。
senses.why: The device is named by shortening the technical word for wireless communication, so the machine carries the name of the method.
senses.whyCN: 这台设备的名字是「无线通信」这一技术词的缩略，因此机器承袭了方法的名字。

senses.title: Broadcasting by radio waves
senses.definition: the activity or service of sending sound to many listeners at once
senses.definitionCN: 把声音同时发送给许多听众的活动或服务
senses.example: The interview will be on the radio tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 这段采访今晚会在广播里播出。
senses.why: Once sound could travel without wires, broadcasting became a public service, and English called it simply the radio.
senses.whyCN: 声音既能不用电线传播，广播便成了公共服务，英语就径直称之为 the radio。

senses.title: Wireless communication technology
senses.definition: the technology of sending signals through space by electromagnetic waves
senses.definitionCN: 通过电磁波在空间中发送信号的技术
senses.example: The message was sent by radio from the ship.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息是用船上的无线电发出的。
senses.why: This is the broadest sense: the physical method itself, used by ships, aircraft and stations alike.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽泛的一层：指这种物理方法本身，船只、飞机与电台都在使用。

senses.title: To send a message by radio
senses.definition: to communicate with someone by radio, especially in an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 用无线电与某人联络，尤指在紧急情况下
senses.example: The pilot radioed for help as the fog closed in.
senses.exampleCN: 雾合拢上来时，飞行员用无线电求救。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, naming the act of sending a message through the same technology.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，指通过同一技术发送消息这一动作。

intro.en: Radio is a shortened form of words built on the Latin word for ray; the technology of wireless signalling took the name of the rays it uses.
intro.cn: radio 是建立在拉丁语表示射线的词之上的词语的缩略；无线通信技术采用了它所使用的那种射线的名字。

items.en: Radius meant a spoke or a ray, a straight line sent out from a centre.
items.cn: radius 指辐条或射线，即从中心射出的一条直线。

items.en: Radiare meant to send out rays, and the stem radi- entered scientific language as a combining form.
items.cn: radiare 意为发出射线，词干 radi- 作为构词成分进入科学语言。

items.en: Early wireless signalling was called radiotelegraphy, sending telegraph messages by electromagnetic waves.
items.cn: 早期的无线通信被称为 radiotelegraphy，即用电磁波发送电报。

items.en: English speakers shortened the long technical word to radio in the early twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，英语使用者把这个冗长的技术词缩略为 radio。

items.en: Modern English uses radio for the device, the broadcast service, the technology and the act of signalling.
items.cn: 现代英语用 radio 指设备、广播服务、技术以及发送信号的行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of rays; the near-meaning group gathers words for broadcasting and wireless signalling.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「射线」词干上的词；近义组收表示广播与无线通信的词。

entries.definition: A detection system using reflected radio waves.
entries.definitionCN: 利用反射无线电波进行探测的系统。

entries.definition: A line from the centre of a circle to its edge.
entries.definitionCN: 从圆心到圆周的一条线。

entries.definition: Energy sent out as waves or particles.
entries.definitionCN: 以波或粒子形式发出的能量。

entries.definition: A person who works with radio equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 从事无线电设备工作的人。

entries.definition: To send sound or pictures to many receivers.
entries.definitionCN: 把声音或图像发送给许多接收者。

entries.definition: Working without connecting wires.
entries.definitionCN: 不通过连接导线工作的。

entries.definition: A device that picks up transmitted signals.
entries.definitionCN: 接收所传送信号的装置。

entries.definition: The sending out of signals or power.
entries.definitionCN: 信号或能量的发送。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin ray in modern dress: wireless signalling was named after the rays that carry it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是穿上现代外衣的拉丁语「射线」：无线通信以承载它的射线命名。

normal.en: Radio, radius and radiation all begin with the Latin word for a ray leaving a centre.
normal.cn: radio、radius 与 radiation 都从拉丁语表示「从中心射出的射线」一词开始。

normal.en: On the radio names the service, while a radio names the box on the kitchen table.
normal.cn: on the radio 指广播服务，而 a radio 指厨房桌上的那台机器。

normal.en: Radio silence means no signals are being sent, often by a ship or an aircraft that must stay unheard.
normal.cn: radio silence 指不发送任何信号，常是船只或飞机必须保持静默时。

normal.en: To radio someone is to send a message by radio rather than by phone.
normal.cn: to radio 某人就是用无线电而不是电话发送消息。

normal.en: Radar is radio detection and ranging, a child of the same technology.
normal.cn: radar 是无线电探测与测距，是同一技术的产物。

abstract.en: Radio made a voice present in millions of rooms at once, the first everyday experience of shared listening.
abstract.cn: 广播让一个声音同时出现在千万个房间里，这是人们第一次日常体验到共同收听。

abstract.en: A device named after invisible rays taught people to trust what they could hear but not see.
abstract.cn: 一台以看不见的射线命名的机器，教会人们去相信听得到却看不见的东西。

abstract.en: Radio silence is powerful because absence of signal is also a message.
abstract.cn: 无线电静默之所以有力，是因为没有信号本身也是一种消息。

examples.en: The radio on the shelf still works after forty years.
examples.cn: 架子上那台收音机用了四十年还能工作。

examples.en: Her talk will be broadcast on the radio this evening.
examples.cn: 她的谈话今晚将在广播中播出。

examples.en: The coast guard radioed the fishing boat to warn it of the storm.
examples.cn: 海岸警卫队用无线电通知渔船有暴风雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞迪欧」——声音不用电线，像射线一样飘进屋里，记住 radio 是收音机、无线电。

root: 拉丁语 radius（射线、辐条）→ radiare（发出射线）→ 科学构词成分 radi- → radiotelegraphy → 缩略为英语 radio；同族有 radar、radiation、radius。

sensesIntro.en: The core is signalling by rays; the senses divide into the receiving device, the broadcast service, the technology and the act of sending a message.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「靠射线传信」；义项分为接收设备、广播服务、技术本身，以及发送消息的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old radio's needle resting on a dial, its speaker faintly warm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台老式收音机的指针停在刻度盘上，扬声器微微发热。

branches.en: a dial turned by a thumb
branches.cn: 拇指转动的刻度盘

branches.en: a voice filling a kitchen
branches.cn: 填满厨房的一个声音

branches.en: an aerial on a ship's roof
branches.cn: 船顶的一根天线

branches.en: a message sent through fog
branches.cn: 穿过雾发出去的一条消息

branches.en: the same signal, once as a machine and once as a programme
branches.cn: 同一个信号，一次是机器，一次是节目

intro.en: The word is a modern shortening of a scientific compound built on the Latin stem for ray, with English endings for people and instruments.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「射线」词干上的科学复合词的现代缩略，加上表示人与器械的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem radi- is shared with radius and radiation, and it still builds new technical words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 radi- 与 radius、radiation 共用，至今仍在构成新的技术词。

definition_zh: 放射性的；具放射性的；受放射性污染的
definition_en: emitting ionizing radiation because atomic nuclei are unstable, or relating to such emission
core_image: 一块泛着幽绿光的矿石旁边，盖革计数器的指针猛然跳起
scene: 这里指「放射性的」。 Uranium ore is radioactive, so it must be handled behind thick shielding.
sceneCN: 这里 radioactive 指「具放射性的」（第 1 个义项：原子核不稳定而自发发出电离辐射）；因此铀矿石必须在厚屏蔽后处理。图中可辨识物件：铀矿石、盖革计数器、辐射标志、铅手套。

pos.zh: 放射性的；具放射性的；与放射性有关的；受放射性污染的
放射性物质（多见于 radioactive(s) 的旧式说法）

derivatives.zh: 放射性；放射现象
辐射；放射线
由放射性衰变产生的
放射性同位素
放射性核素

senses.title: Emitting ionizing radiation
senses.titleCN: 具放射性的：原子核不稳定自发发出射线
senses.definition: giving off ionizing radiation because the atomic nuclei are unstable
senses.definitionCN: 因原子核不稳定而发出电离辐射
senses.example: Uranium ore is radioactive and sets off a Geiger counter.
senses.exampleCN: 铀矿石具有放射性，会让盖革计数器响起。
senses.why: The adjective joins radio- 'ray' to active 'doing': the material is actively giving out rays rather than merely reflecting them.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把表示「射线」的 radio- 与表示「起作用的」active 结合起来：材料在主动发出射线，而不只是反射射线。

senses.title: Relating to the phenomenon
senses.titleCN: 放射性现象的：用作技术修饰语
senses.definition: used in technical phrases to name the process or property of emitting rays
senses.definitionCN: 在技术短语中命名发射射线的过程或性质
senses.example: Radioactive decay follows a fixed half-life for each isotope.
senses.exampleCN: 每种同位素的放射性衰变都遵循固定的半衰期。
senses.why: Once the noun radioactivity was coined, the adjective became the general label for anything belonging to that phenomenon.
senses.whyCN: radioactivity 这一名词出现后，形容词便成为指属该现象的一般标签。

senses.title: Contaminated by radioactive material
senses.titleCN: 受放射性污染的：沾上了放射性物质
senses.definition: made dangerous by contact with radioactive material rather than by its own nuclei
senses.definitionCN: 因接触放射性物质而变得危险，而不是自身原子核不稳定
senses.example: The scrap yard was declared radioactive after the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏之后，这家废料场被宣布受到放射性污染。
senses.why: Contamination spreads the label from the source to whatever the material touches, so objects can be radioactive without being radioactive substances.
senses.whyCN: 污染把这个标签从源头传播到材料接触过的一切，因此物品可以「受放射性污染」而本身并不是放射性物质。

senses.title: Of an unstable isotope
senses.titleCN: 放射性同位素的：指不稳定核素
senses.definition: describing an isotope whose nuclei decay spontaneously, often used before isotope or element names
senses.definitionCN: 形容原子核自发衰变的同位素，常用于 isotope 或元素名称之前
senses.example: Carbon-14 is the radioactive isotope used to date organic remains.
senses.exampleCN: 碳-14 是用来给有机遗存定年的放射性同位素。
senses.why: Chemistry distinguishes stable from unstable isotopes with this adjective, keeping the physical meaning close to the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 化学用这个形容词区分稳定与不稳定同位素，其物理含义紧贴第一义项。

senses.title: Used for dating
senses.titleCN: 用于定年：靠衰变速度推算年代
senses.definition: in geology and archaeology, describing a method that measures the decay of isotopes to estimate age
senses.definitionCN: 在地质学与考古学中，形容通过测量同位素衰变来估算年代的方法
senses.example: Radioactive dating placed the rock at about 2.5 billion years.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性定年把这层岩石测定在约 25 亿年前。
senses.why: Because decay runs at a steady rate, a radioactive clock can be read long after the event, and the adjective names that clock.
senses.whyCN: 由于衰变速率稳定，放射性时钟在事件发生很久之后仍可读数，形容词命名的正是这只钟。

senses.title: Associated with nuclear waste
senses.titleCN: 与核废料相关的：长期危险的工业产物
senses.definition: describing waste from reactors or weapons programmes that stays hazardous for a very long time
senses.definitionCN: 形容反应堆或核武器计划产生的、长期保持危险的废物
senses.example: Radioactive waste must be stored deep underground for thousands of years.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性废物必须深埋地下，存放数千年。
senses.why: The nuclear industry extended the adjective to its by-products, where the danger lasts far longer than any human schedule.
senses.whyCN: 核工业把这个形容词扩展到其副产品，那里的危险远超任何人类时间表。

senses.title: Used as a tracer
senses.titleCN: 作示踪剂用的：让射线替人「看见」路径
senses.definition: describing a small amount of radioactive material used to follow movement through a body, pipe or plant
senses.definitionCN: 形容少量用于追踪物质在人体、管道或植物中运动的放射性材料
senses.example: A radioactive tracer showed where the fluid leaked from the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性示踪剂显示出液体从管道何处泄漏。
senses.why: The emitted rays act as a signal, so a tiny amount of radioactive substance can reveal a path without being seen directly.
senses.whyCN: 发出的射线充当信号，因此极少量放射性物质无需直接可见也能暴露路径。

senses.title: Figuratively explosive
senses.titleCN: 比喻上「带辐射」的：碰不得的敏感议题
senses.definition: in informal speech, describing a topic or person so controversial that others avoid touching it
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容某话题或人物争议极大，别人都避而远之
senses.example: The old lawsuit became politically radioactive during the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 那桩旧诉讼在竞选期间变成了政治上碰不得的议题。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the idea of invisible danger: as with real radioactivity, harm may follow mere contact, so people keep their distance.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了「看不见的危险」：如同真实放射性，仅仅接触就可能受害，于是人们保持距离。

intro.en: Radioactive is a modern compound of radio- 'ray' and active, coined at the end of the nineteenth century when rays from uranium were first studied. Elements of the history remain uncertain.
intro.cn: radioactive 是 radio-「射线」与 active 的现代复合词，在 19 世纪末人们开始研究铀射线时被造出。其历史细节仍有存疑处。

items.en: The combining form radio- goes back to Latin radius 'spoke, ray'. It entered modern science through words for rays and radiant energy.
items.cn: 构词成分 radio- 可追溯到拉丁 radius「辐条、光线」，经由指射线与辐射能的科学词汇进入现代用语。

items.en: Active comes from Latin activus, built on agere 'to do, drive'. The pair radio- + active literally suggests 'actively ray-emitting'.
items.cn: active 出自拉丁 activus，基于 agere「做、驱动」。radio- 与 active 的组合字面上就是「主动发出射线的」。

items.en: The compound radio-active is generally attributed to Marie Curie's circle in 1898, in the period when polonium and radium were being isolated. The precise first printed use is uncertain.
items.cn: 复合词 radio-active 一般认为出自 1898 年前后居里夫妇的圈子，正值分离钋与镭的时期。最早的印刷使用确切出处存疑。

items.en: English quickly adopted radioactive for any substance giving off such rays, and radioactivity was formed as its noun.
items.cn: 英语很快用 radioactive 指任何发出这类射线的物质，并构成名词 radioactivity。

items.en: During the twentieth century the word spread from physics to medicine, industry, waste management and dating methods.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词从物理学扩展到医学、工业、废物管理与定年方法。

items.en: Attribution of the coinage is generally accepted rather than documented in every detail, and the exact first English citation remains uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（创造归属与首见书证）：该词的创造归属属于「一般认为是」，并非每个细节都有文献可证；英语最早书证也仍存疑。

note.en: The first group separates adjectives and nouns of the same ray-family; the second gives near-synonyms for danger or instability.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一「射线词族」中的形容词与名词；第二组给出表示危险或不稳定的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating to radiation as a mode of energy transfer, especially heat. It says nothing about unstable nuclei or contamination.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为能量传递方式（尤指传热）的辐射，与原子核不稳定或污染无关。

entries.definition: The energy or rays themselves. Radioactive describes the source; radiation is what leaves it.
entries.definitionCN: 指能量或射线本身。radioactive 描述源头，radiation 指离开源头的东西。

entries.definition: The property or process of emitting rays. It cannot stand before a noun the way radioactive can.
entries.definitionCN: 指发出射线的性质或过程，不能像 radioactive 那样直接放在名词前。

entries.definition: The everyday word for broadcast communication or its equipment, shortened from radiotelegraphy; not a synonym for radioactive.
entries.definitionCN: 指广播通信或其设备的日常词，由 radiotelegraphy 缩略而来，并非 radioactive 的同义词。

entries.definition: In nuclear slang, 'hot' means radioactive or highly contaminated. It is informal and depends on context.
entries.definitionCN: 在核工业俚语中，hot 指具放射性或污染严重的；属口语用法，且依赖语境。

entries.definition: Describing a nucleus that may decay. Unstable states the cause; radioactive states the observable emission.
entries.definitionCN: 形容可能衰变的原子核。unstable 说的是原因，radioactive 说的是可观测的发射现象。

entries.definition: Made impure by contact with a harmful substance. It can be chemical or radioactive, so it is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 因接触有害物质而变得不纯；可以指化学污染，也可指放射性污染，范围更宽。

entries.definition: Relating to atomic nuclei or nuclear energy. A nuclear plant may handle radioactive material, but nuclear itself does not mean 'emitting rays'.
entries.definitionCN: 与原子核或核能有关。核电站会处理放射性物质，但 nuclear 本身不表示「发出射线」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: radio- 'ray' + active 'doing': the material is doing rays.
normal.cn: radio-「射线」+ active「起作用的」：材料在「做射线」。

normal.en: The family runs radioactivity, radiation, radioisotope, radionuclide, radiogenic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 radioactivity、radiation、radioisotope、radionuclide、radiogenic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: radioactive decay, radioactive waste, radioactive dating, radioactive tracer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：放射性衰变、放射性废物、放射性定年、放射性示踪剂。

normal.en: A Geiger counter clicks because the rays ionize gas inside it.
normal.cn: 盖革计数器会响，是因为射线电离了管内的气体。

normal.en: radiative is about heat transfer; radioactive is about unstable nuclei.
normal.cn: radiative 讲传热，radioactive 讲不稳定原子核。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that keeps warm by itself, never needing a fire, because the heat is made inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块不用火也一直温热的石头，因为热从它内部产生。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible drizzle falling from a rock, which only a clicking meter can hear.
abstract.cn: 想象一场自岩石落下的无形细雨，只有会咔哒响的仪表听得见。

abstract.en: Picture a warning sign painted on a box that no one dares to open.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子被画上警示标志，没人敢打开。

examples.en: Naturally radioactive rocks release radon gas into basements.
examples.cn: 天然放射性岩石会向地下室释放氡气。

examples.en: The laboratory stores radioactive waste in lead-lined containers.
examples.cn: 实验室把放射性废物存放在衬铅容器里。

examples.en: Investigators used a radioactive tracer to locate the underground leak.
examples.cn: 调查人员用放射性示踪剂定位地下泄漏点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「射线（radio）一直在动（active）」——不停向外发出射线 → radioactive 放射性的

root: 拉丁 radius「光线、辐条」+ activus「活动的」（agere「做」）；1898 年前后由 radio- 与 active 合成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the physical property to its uses: unstable nuclei emit rays, and that emission becomes a hazard, a clock, a tracer, a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从物理性质走向各种用途：不稳定核发出射线，而这一发射又变成危害、时钟、示踪剂与比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green-glowing ore making a meter needle jump.
core.cn: 核心意象：泛绿光的矿石让仪表指针猛跳。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY: unstable nuclei emit ionizing rays, and the adjective names that process.
branches.cn: 性质本身：不稳定核发出电离射线，形容词命名这一过程。

branches.en: SPREAD BY CONTACT: the label moves from the source to whatever touches it.
branches.cn: 接触传播：标签从源头转移到它接触过的一切。

branches.en: THE ISOTOPE: chemistry uses the adjective to separate stable from unstable nuclear species.
branches.cn: 同位素：化学用该形容词区分稳定与不稳定的核素。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: steady decay becomes a clock, and emitted rays become a tracer signal.
branches.cn: 工具化：稳定衰变成为时钟，发出的射线成为示踪信号。

branches.en: LONG DANGER: industrial waste keeps the physical hazard, while politics turns it into a metaphor.
branches.cn: 长期危险：工业废物保留物理危害，政治则把它变成比喻。

intro.en: Radioactive is a modern scientific compound: a Latin-derived combining form for rays, plus an adjective of action, with -ity forming its noun.
intro.cn: radioactive 是现代科学复合词：拉丁来源的「射线」构词成分，加上表示动作的形容词，再由 -ity 构成名词。

latinIntro.en: The ray family includes radius, radiate, radiant, radiation, radiator and radio; the 'do' family includes act, action, agent, active and actor. Radioactive sits where the two families meet.
latinIntro.cn: 射线词族包括 radius、radiate、radiant、radiation、radiator、radio；「做」词族包括 act、action、agent、active、actor。radioactive 正处在这两个词族的交会处。

items.example: The isotope is radioactive for thousands of years.
items.exampleCN: 该同位素在数千年内保持放射性。

items.meaning: the property of emitting such rays
items.example: Radioactivity was discovered before its cause was understood.
items.exampleCN: 放射性的发现早于人们理解其成因。

items.meaning: the rays sent out, or the act of sending them
items.example: Radiation from the sample was measured hourly.
items.exampleCN: 每小时测量一次样品的辐射。

items.meaning: to send rays out from a centre
items.example: The metal radiated heat long after the fire died.
items.exampleCN: 火熄灭很久后，金属仍在散发热量。

items.example: The lab ordered a short-lived radioisotope.
items.exampleCN: 实验室订购了一种短寿命放射性同位素。
不同放射性核素的半衰期差别很大。

items.example: Radiogenic heat keeps the mantle slowly moving.
items.exampleCN: 放射性成因热使地幔缓慢流动。

items.example: The mail was irradiated as a precaution.
items.exampleCN: 邮件经过辐照作为预防措施。

definition_zh: 暴怒；狂怒；风行；狂热
definition_en: very strong anger; to speak or act with violent anger; to continue with great force or popularity; a widespread enthusiasm or fashion
core_image: 被砸裂的车门，玻璃上还留着拳印
scene: 停车场里，两名司机为抢一个车位大声争吵，其中一人一拳砸在车门上。He flew into a rage when another car took the space he had waited for.
sceneCN: 这里 rage 是「暴怒」（第 1 个义项：极其强烈的愤怒）；句意为另一辆车抢走了他等候的车位，他顿时暴怒。画面里可留意：裂开的车门、还留着的拳印、围观的司机。

pos.zh: 暴怒；狂热；风行
狂怒；怒斥；（风暴、时尚）猛烈持续

derivatives.zh: rage 加 -ing，指狂怒的，也指猛烈的，如 raging storm
en- 加 rage，指使某人暴怒
rage 加 -ful，指充满怒气的

senses.title: Very strong anger
senses.definition: a feeling of violent and uncontrolled anger
senses.definitionCN: 一种猛烈而失控的愤怒
senses.example: He slammed the door in a rage.
senses.exampleCN: 他暴怒之下摔上门。
senses.why: Latin rabies meant madness, and the French word built on it named a fury so strong it looked like madness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rabies 意为疯狂，建立其上的法语词指一种强烈到近乎疯狂的愤怒。

senses.title: To act with violent anger
senses.definition: to speak or behave with violent anger
senses.definitionCN: 带着猛烈怒气说话或行动
senses.example: She raged at the driver for several minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那名司机怒吼了好几分钟。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, naming the outward behaviour that anger produces rather than the feeling alone.
senses.whyCN: 名词化为动词，指愤怒所产生的外在行为，而不只是感受本身。

senses.title: To continue with great force
senses.definition: to continue violently or spread widely, used of storms, wars and fashions
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈地持续或广泛蔓延，用于风暴、战争与时尚
senses.example: The storm raged all night along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨沿海岸肆虐了一整夜。
senses.why: Anger that cannot be stopped looks like a storm that cannot be stopped, so the word was applied to any force that will not calm.
senses.whyCN: 无法平息的愤怒像无法平息的风暴，于是这个词被用到任何不肯平静的力量上。

senses.title: A widespread fashion
senses.definition: a short period when something is extremely popular
senses.definitionCN: 某事物极受欢迎的短暂时段
senses.example: The new game became a rage among teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新游戏在青少年中风靡一时。
senses.why: A fashion that spreads fast and refuses to be quiet was called a rage, as if enthusiasm were a storm.
senses.whyCN: 一种迅速蔓延、不肯安静的时尚被称作 rage，仿佛热情也是一场风暴。

intro.en: Rage comes through French from the Latin word for madness, and the sense of fury grew from the image of a mind driven out of its normal state.
intro.cn: rage 经法语来自拉丁语表示疯狂的名词，暴怒义从「心智被逐出常态」这一画面生长出来。

items.en: Rabies meant madness or frenzy, and in medicine it also named the disease that causes violent distress.
items.cn: rabies 意为疯狂、狂乱，在医学上也指引起剧烈痛苦的那种疾病。

items.en: The related verb meant to rave or be mad, describing a person beside themselves with feeling.
items.cn: 相关动词意为狂乱、发疯，形容一个人情绪激动到失去常态。

items.en: Old French rage named furious anger and also the violent force of a storm or a disease.
items.cn: 古法语 rage 既指狂怒，也指风暴或疾病的猛烈力量。

items.en: Middle English rage kept both the anger and the storm, so the word could describe a person and a sea.
items.cn: 中古英语的 rage 同时保留了怒气与风暴，所以这个词既能形容人，也能形容海。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of a fashion that sweeps a group, as if enthusiasm were weather.
items.cn: 现代英语又增添了「席卷群体的时尚」这一义，仿佛热情也是天气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same word and its Latin relative; the near-meaning group gathers words for anger and frenzy.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个词的形式及其拉丁亲属；近义组收表示愤怒与狂乱的词。

entries.definition: A viral disease that causes madness in animals.
entries.definitionCN: 使动物发狂的病毒性疾病。

entries.definition: Violent and out of control.
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈而失控的。

entries.definition: To make someone very angry.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人极为愤怒。

entries.definition: Great anger caused by something unfair, a different formation.
entries.definitionCN: 因不公之事引起的强烈愤慨，构词方式不同。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of displeasure.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的不快情绪。

entries.definition: Wild and violent anger.
entries.definitionCN: 狂野而猛烈的愤怒。

entries.definition: Deep anger, often in a literary or religious tone.
entries.definitionCN: 深重的愤怒，常带文学或宗教语气。

entries.definition: A state of wild uncontrolled activity.
entries.definitionCN: 狂乱失控的状态。

normalIntro.en: The word is madness made social: a feeling, a behaviour, a storm and a fashion all move with the same violence.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把疯狂放进社会：感受、行为、风暴与时尚都以同一种猛烈推进。

normal.en: Rage and rabies share the Latin word for madness, which is why rage feels like something that takes over the body.
normal.cn: rage 与 rabies 共用拉丁语「疯狂」一词，所以暴怒感觉像有东西占据了身体。

normal.en: Fly into a rage is the fixed phrase for anger that arrives suddenly, as if the person were airborne.
normal.cn: fly into a rage 是形容怒气突然降临的固定说法，仿佛人被吹了起来。

normal.en: Road rage names anger that grows inside a car and then escapes through the window.
normal.cn: road rage 指在车里积蓄、再从车窗里泄出的怒气。

normal.en: All the rage means extremely fashionable, as if the fashion were a storm passing through.
normal.cn: all the rage 意为极其时髦，仿佛时尚是一场过境的风暴。

normal.en: A raging storm and a raging man use the same participle, because neither can be calmed quickly.
normal.cn: raging storm 与 raging man 用同一个分词，因为两者都无法迅速平息。

abstract.en: Anger and weather share one word because both are forces people can only wait out.
abstract.cn: 愤怒与天气共用一个词，因为两者都是人们只能等待其过去的力。

abstract.en: A fashion called a rage is a reminder that enthusiasm can behave like a storm and disappear just as fast.
abstract.cn: 被称为 rage 的时尚提醒我们：热情可以像风暴一样出现，也能同样快地消失。

abstract.en: To rage is to insist that the world match your sense of what is right, and the cost is often borne by whoever is nearest.
abstract.cn: 狂怒就是坚持世界必须符合你的是非感，而代价往往由最近的人承担。

examples.en: She was shaking with rage after the meeting.
examples.cn: 会议结束后，她气得发抖。

examples.en: The storm raged for three days without a pause.
examples.cn: 暴风雨一连肆虐了三天没有停歇。

examples.en: Short jackets were all the rage that spring.
examples.cn: 那个春天短款外套风靡一时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞吉」——怒气像锐利的针扎进来，一下就爆，记住 rage 是暴怒。

root: 拉丁语 rabies（疯狂）→ rabere（发狂）→ 古法语 rage → 英语 rage；同族有 raging、enrage，以及同源的 rabies。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fury near madness; the senses divide into the feeling, its outward action, unstoppable force and a fashion that sweeps through.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「近乎疯狂的暴怒」；义项分为这种感受、它的外在行动、不可阻挡的力量，以及席卷而来的时尚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a car door with a fist-shaped dent in the metal.
core.cn: 核心意象：车门上留着一个拳头形状的凹痕。

chain: A STORM THAT WILL NOT STOP

branches.en: a door slammed hard enough to shake
branches.cn: 摔得整扇门都在晃

branches.en: a voice raised at a stranger
branches.cn: 冲着陌生人抬高的嗓音

branches.en: waves hitting a sea wall all night
branches.cn: 整夜拍打海堤的浪

branches.en: a game everyone suddenly plays
branches.cn: 突然人人都在玩的游戏

branches.en: the same violence, once in a person and once in weather
branches.cn: 同一种猛烈，一次在人身上，一次在天气里

intro.en: The word came through French from the Latin noun for madness, and English built its relatives with participles and a prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语表示疯狂的名词，英语用分词与一个前缀构成它的亲属词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun rabies survives in English as the name of the disease it also described.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 rabies 在英语中存活下来，成为它所描述的那种疾病的名字。

definition_zh: 降雨；降雨量；一场雨
definition_en: rain falling from the sky, or the amount of rain measured over a period
core_image: 云底压得很低，雨线密密地垂到地面，量筒里的水一寸寸升高
scene: 雨下了一整夜，气象站的量筒里积起半尺深的水。Heavy rainfall overnight raised the water in the gauge by half a foot.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「落下的雨水」（第 1 个义项：降雨这一事件）；句意为夜间的大雨使量筒里的水升高了半英尺。

pos.zh: 降雨；降雨量；（一场）雨

forms.label: 复数（多场降雨或多次读数）

derivatives.zh: 雨；下雨
多雨的
降雨格局
降雨总量
降水（涵盖雨雪冰雹）

senses.title: Rain coming down
senses.definition: the fall of rain from clouds
senses.definitionCN: 雨从云中落下这一事件
senses.example: Heavy rainfall overnight raised the water in the gauge by half a foot.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间的大雨使量筒里的水升高了半英尺。
senses.why: Rain plus fall names the event directly: the first element is the substance, the second is its motion.
senses.whyCN: rain 加 fall 直接命名事件：前者是物质，后者是它的运动。

senses.title: The measured depth
senses.definition: the depth of rain that has fallen, measured in millimetres or inches
senses.definitionCN: 已经落下的雨的深度，以毫米或英寸计
senses.example: The city recorded forty millimetres of rainfall in one hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市一小时内记录到四十毫米降雨量。
senses.why: A gauge converts a shower into a depth, and the compound takes on that measured reading.
senses.whyCN: 量筒把一场雨变成一段深度，这个复合词也就承担了这一读数。

senses.title: The yearly total
senses.definition: the total rain a place receives in a year
senses.definitionCN: 某地一年所获得的总雨量
senses.example: The island's annual rainfall supports dense forest.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的年降雨量足以养活茂密的森林。
senses.why: Climate description needs a period, so rainfall becomes an annual figure rather than a single storm.
senses.whyCN: 气候描述需要一个周期，于是 rainfall 成为年度数字，而不是一场暴雨。

senses.title: A season's rain
senses.definition: the rain belonging to a particular season or month
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个季节或月份的雨
senses.example: Most of the region's rainfall arrives between June and September.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区大部分降雨集中在六月到九月之间。
senses.why: Once totals are grouped by month, the word also names the rain attached to a stretch of the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 一旦总量按月分组，这个词也指附着在某段日历上的雨水。

senses.title: Water supply for farming
senses.definition: rain considered as the water source for crops and pastures
senses.definitionCN: 被视为作物与牧场水源的雨水
senses.example: Dry farming depends entirely on natural rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 旱作农业完全依赖自然降雨。
senses.why: For a farmer, rain is not weather but input; the word shifts from the sky to the water budget.
senses.whyCN: 对农民来说，雨不是天气而是投入；这个词于是从天空转到水量收支。

senses.title: Liquid precipitation as a category
senses.definition: in climate science, the liquid form of precipitation as opposed to snow
senses.definitionCN: 气候科学中与降雪相对的液态降水
senses.example: The model separates rainfall from snowfall in mountain zones.
senses.exampleCN: 模型在山地分区中把降雨与降雪分开处理。
senses.why: Classification needs a label for the liquid member, and rainfall supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要给液态成员一个标签，rainfall 提供了这个标签。

senses.title: Rain in a particular place
senses.definition: the characteristic rain of a named region, as in tropical or coastal rainfall
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定地区的典型雨水，如热带或沿海降雨
senses.example: Coastal rainfall keeps the valleys green long into summer.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海降雨让山谷一直绿到盛夏。
senses.why: Place adjectives attach naturally, because rain is one of the first things people notice about a region.
senses.whyCN: 地点形容词自然附着其上，因为雨是人最先注意到的地方特征之一。

senses.title: Rain produced by cloud seeding
senses.definition: rain that has been encouraged to fall by human intervention
senses.definitionCN: 经人工干预而促使其落下的雨
senses.example: The province counts on seeded rainfall during drought years.
senses.exampleCN: 该省在干旱年份依靠人工增雨。
senses.why: When people can trigger the fall, the same noun names the product of an intervention.
senses.whyCN: 当人能触发这场落下时，同一个名词也指干预的产物。

intro.en: Rainfall is a modern English compound of two native Old English words. The compound itself is recent, while both halves are ancient. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: rainfall 是由两个英语本土的古英语词构成的现代复合词。复合词本身很新，两个构件却很古老。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Rain goes back to Old English regn, from Proto-Germanic *regna-, a word shared by most Germanic languages.
items.cn: rain 源自古英语 regn，出自原始日耳曼语 *regna-，为多数日耳曼语言共有。

items.en: Fall goes back to Old English feallan 'to fall', from Proto-Germanic *fallan, and has always meant a downward movement.
items.cn: fall 源自古英语 feallan「落下」，出自原始日耳曼语 *fallan，一直表示向下的运动。

items.en: The compound rainfall appears in nineteenth-century writing, when weather observation became systematic and totals needed a short name.
items.cn: 复合词 rainfall 出现于十九世纪文献，当时天气观测走向系统化，总量需要一个简短名称。

items.en: Rain gauges and agricultural yearbooks spread the measured sense, so that a place could be described by how much rainfall it received rather than by how often it rained.
items.cn: 雨量筒与农业年鉴推广了测量义，于是描述一个地方可以靠它接收多少降雨量，而不是靠下雨的次数。

items.en: The measured sense expanded with national weather services and the phrase annual rainfall became standard in geography textbooks.
items.cn: 随着国家气象机构的建立，其测量义扩展，annual rainfall 成为地理教科书的固定说法。

note.en: Group one holds compounds built on the same word rain; group two holds words for water falling in other ways.
note.cn: 第一组是以同一个 rain 构成的复合词；第二组是表示水以其他方式落下的词。

entries.definition: A single drop of rain; it names one piece, while rainfall names the whole event or total.
entries.definitionCN: 一滴雨；它指单个水滴，而 rainfall 指整个事件或总量。

entries.definition: The coloured arc seen when sunlight passes through drops; it is a sight caused by rain, not the rain itself.
entries.definitionCN: 阳光穿过水滴时看到的彩色弧；它是雨造成的景象，而不是雨本身。

entries.definition: A storm with heavy rain; it adds the idea of wind and violence that rainfall does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 夹带大雨的风暴；它多了风与猛烈之意，而 rainfall 没有这层意思。

entries.definition: Falling water of every kind, including snow and hail; it is the technical category to which rainfall belongs.
entries.definitionCN: 各种形式落下的水，包括雪与冰雹；它是 rainfall 所属的技术类别。

entries.definition: Very light rain made of tiny drops; it describes an intensity, not an amount over a season.
entries.definitionCN: 由细小水滴构成的毛毛雨；它描述强度，而非一段时间内的总量。

entries.definition: A sudden heavy fall of rain; it stresses the burst, while rainfall can be calm and cumulative.
entries.definitionCN: 突然而降的大雨；它强调爆发，而 rainfall 可以是平缓累积的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the compound is transparent, and its partners are real weather terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个复合词的意义一目了然，搭配也都是真实的天气术语。

normal.en: rain + fall: the substance plus its motion, exactly like snowfall and moonlight.
normal.cn: rain + fall：物质加运动，与 snowfall、moonlight 完全同构。

normal.en: rainfall total is the phrase used when the event is converted into a number.
normal.cn: rainfall total 是把事件换算成数字时使用的搭配。

normal.en: annual rainfall is the standard geography phrase for a place's yearly water supply.
normal.cn: annual rainfall 是地理学中描述某地年度水量的标准说法。

normal.en: rainfall and snowfall split the same idea by temperature, and precipitation is the umbrella term.
normal.cn: rainfall 与 snowfall 按温度把同一想法分开，precipitation 则是统称。

normal.en: rain gauge is the instrument that turns rainfall into a reading, pairing the compound with its tool.
normal.cn: rain gauge 是把 rainfall 变成读数的仪器，把这个复合词与工具配在一起。

abstract.en: Abstractly, rainfall is water leaving the sky on a schedule no one controls; the compound names both the leaving and the amount left behind.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，rainfall 是按无人能控制的日程离开天空的水；这个复合词同时命名离开与留下的量。

abstract.en: The same word can be a moment (a heavy fall) or a decade (an annual average), because a gauge can measure either.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可是一刻（一场大雨），也可是十年（年均值），因为量筒两者都能测。

abstract.en: So rainfall is rain viewed as supply: something that arrives, accumulates and must be counted.
abstract.cn: 所以 rainfall 是把雨看作供给：它到来、累积，并且必须被计量。

examples.en: The northern slope receives twice the rainfall of the southern slope.
examples.cn: 北坡的降雨量是南坡的两倍。

examples.en: A week of steady rainfall replenished the reservoirs.
examples.cn: 一周持续的降雨补足了水库。

examples.en: Gardeners time their planting by the expected rainfall.
examples.cn: 园丁按预期的降雨安排种植时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: rain（雨）+ fall（落下）：雨从天上落下来 → rainfall 降雨、降雨量

root: rain 源自古英语 regn（原始日耳曼语 *regna-），fall 源自古英语 feallan（原始日耳曼语 *fallan）；复合词 rainfall 于十九世纪出现。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow water from sky to ledger: the event of falling, the depth measured, the yearly total, the seasonal share, the farm supply, the liquid category, the regional character and the artificially seeded shower.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让水从天空走到账本：落下的事件、测得的深度、全年总量、季节份额、农业供给、液态类别、地方特征以及人工催下的雨。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water leaves the sky and is caught, first as an event and then as a depth in a gauge.
core.cn: 核心意象：水离开天空并被接住，先是一个事件，然后成为量筒里的一段深度。

branches.en: EVENT AND READING: the shower and the number it leaves in the gauge are one noun.
branches.cn: 事件与读数：一场雨与它在量筒里留下的数字共用一个名词。

branches.en: CALENDAR: grouped by season or by year, rain becomes a schedule.
branches.cn: 日历：按季节或按年份分组，雨就变成一张时间表。

branches.en: SUPPLY: for farming, the same water is an input in the budget.
branches.cn: 供给：对农业而言，同一份水是收支表里的投入。

branches.en: CATEGORY: climate science sets the liquid member beside snow.
branches.cn: 类别：气候科学把液态成员与雪并列。

branches.en: PLACE AND INTERVENTION: rain belongs to a region, and can also be made to fall.
branches.cn: 地方与干预：雨属于某个地区，也可以被人为催下。

intro.en: Rainfall is a native compound, so its family grows by compounding rather than by Latin suffixes: rain + drop, bow, coat, storm, water and gauge.
intro.cn: rainfall 是英语本土复合词，其词族靠复合而非拉丁后缀扩展：rain 加 drop、bow、coat、storm、water、gauge。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic, with no Latin ancestor; the Latin entry list is empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: 两个构件都属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁词条列表按设计留空。

items.example: A raindrop splashed on the hot stone.
items.exampleCN: 一滴雨落在滚烫的石头上溅开了。

items.meaning: the coloured arc formed by sunlight in raindrops
items.meaningCN: 阳光在雨滴中形成的彩色弧（bow 指弓形）
items.example: A rainbow rose over the wet field.
items.exampleCN: 湿漉漉的田野上升起一道彩虹。

items.meaning: a waterproof coat worn in rain
items.example: He folded his raincoat into the bag.
items.exampleCN: 他把雨衣折好放进包里。

items.meaning: a storm accompanied by heavy rain
items.example: The rainstorm closed the mountain road.

items.meaning: water that has fallen as rain, often collected for use
items.meaningCN: 落下的雨水，常被收集利用
items.example: The barrel stores rainwater for the garden.
items.exampleCN: 桶里存着浇园用的雨水。

items.example: The rain gauge was read at dawn.

items.meaning: the summed rainfall over a period
items.meaningCN: 一段时间内累计的降雨总量
items.example: The monthly rainfall total broke a record.

items.meaning: rain made acidic by dissolved pollutants
items.meaningCN: 因溶解污染物而呈酸性的雨，即酸雨
items.example: Acid rain stripped the leaves from the trees.

definition_zh: 举起；提高；筹集；抚养；提出；引起
definition_en: to lift something to a higher position; to increase an amount or level; to collect money for a purpose; to bring up children or animals; to put a subject forward for discussion; to cause a feeling or reaction
core_image: 一只举到半空的手，掌心朝前
scene: 会议室里，一位成员把手举到半空，示意想就预算发问。She raised her hand and waited for the chair to notice her.
sceneCN: 这里 raise 是「举起」（第 1 个义项：把某物抬到更高的位置）；句意为她举起手，等主席注意到她。画面里可留意：举到半空的手、朝前的手掌、会议桌。

pos.zh: 举起；提高；筹集；抚养；提出；引起
加薪（美式）；提高

derivatives.zh: raise 加 -er，指筹集者或饲养者
raise 加 -ing，指举起、抚养或筹集的过程
fund 与 raiser 复合，指筹款活动或筹款人

senses.title: To lift to a higher position
senses.definition: to move something upward to a higher place or level
senses.definitionCN: 把某物向上移到更高的位置或水平
senses.example: Raise your hand if you have a question.
senses.exampleCN: 有问题请举手。
senses.why: The word came into English from Old Norse with the plain sense of setting something upright or lifting it, and that physical act is still the centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古诺斯语进入英语，本义是把某物立起或抬起，这个身体动作至今仍是核心。

senses.title: To increase an amount
senses.definition: to make a price, level or amount higher
senses.definitionCN: 使价格、水平或数量变高
senses.example: The shop raised its prices twice this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店今年两次提价。
senses.why: Raising a thing higher and raising a number higher use the same image, so the word moved easily from objects to quantities.
senses.whyCN: 把东西举高与把数字提高用的是同一幅画面，所以这个词从实物轻易地转向了数量。

senses.title: To collect money
senses.definition: to gather money or support for a purpose, often for charity
senses.definitionCN: 为某个目的募集钱款或支持，常指慈善
senses.example: The class raised money for the animal shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 全班为动物收容所筹集了钱款。
senses.why: Money that is brought together and lifted into a common fund looks like something raised up from many hands.
senses.whyCN: 把分散的钱聚拢并抬进一个共同基金，看起来就像从许多只手中把东西举起来。

senses.title: To bring up children or animals
senses.definition: to care for a child or an animal until it is grown
senses.definitionCN: 照料孩子或动物直到长大
senses.example: She raised three children on her own.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自抚养了三个孩子。
senses.why: To raise a child is to lift that person up through years of care, and the same verb serves for animals on a farm.
senses.whyCN: 抚养孩子就是通过多年照料把人「托举」起来，同一个动词也用于农场里的动物。

senses.title: To put a subject forward
senses.definition: to bring a question or subject to other people's attention for discussion
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或话题提到别人面前供讨论
senses.example: He raised a question about the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 他就日程安排提了一个问题。
senses.why: A subject brought into a conversation is lifted into view, so the word of lifting also means to mention for discussion.
senses.whyCN: 被带进对话的话题被举到众人眼前，于是「举起」这个词也指提出来讨论。

senses.title: To cause a feeling or reaction
senses.definition: to produce a feeling, doubt or reaction in people
senses.definitionCN: 在人们心中产生某种感受、疑虑或反应
senses.example: The news raised fears of another delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这则消息引起了对再次延误的担忧。
senses.why: If an action lifts a feeling into notice, it causes that feeling, and this sense extends the word from things to emotions.
senses.whyCN: 一个举动把某种情绪举到众人注意之中，就是引起了那种情绪，这一义项把词从实物扩展到情感。

intro.en: Raise came into English from Old Norse, where the verb meant to set something upright; it is related to rise but carries an object.
intro.cn: raise 从古诺斯语进入英语，那个动词意为把某物立起；它与 rise 相关，但必须带宾语。

items.en: Reisa meant to raise or to set upright, and Norse settlers brought it into northern English.
items.cn: reisa 意为举起或立起，诺斯定居者把它带入英格兰北部。

items.en: Raise and rise come from the same family, but rise is what a thing does and raise is what someone does to it.
items.cn: raise 与 rise 同属一族，但 rise 是事物自身发生的动作，raise 是某人对它施加的动作。

items.en: Middle English raise kept the sense of lifting and setting up, and added the sense of bringing up a child.
items.cn: 中古英语的 raise 保留了举起与竖立的意思，并增加了抚养孩子的义项。

items.en: From lifting objects came lifting prices, collecting money, raising a subject and raising a feeling.
items.cn: 从举物生出提价、筹钱、提出话题与引起情绪等义。

items.en: Modern English uses raise for lifting, increasing, collecting, nurturing, mentioning and causing, and as a noun for a pay increase.
items.cn: 现代英语用 raise 表示举起、增加、筹集、养育、提及与引起，并作名词指加薪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of lifting and increasing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根上的形式；近义组收表示举起与增加的动词。

entries.definition: To go upward by itself, without an object.
entries.definitionCN: 自身向上移动，不带宾语。

entries.definition: To begin to exist, especially of a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 开始出现，尤指问题。

entries.definition: A person or thing that raises.
entries.definitionCN: 举起或筹集的人或物。

entries.definition: The act of lifting, collecting or bringing up.
entries.definitionCN: 举起、筹集或抚养的行为。

entries.definition: To move something upward with effort.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地把某物向上移动。

entries.definition: To make or become larger in amount.
entries.definitionCN: 使数量变大或变大。

entries.definition: To gather things or money together.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西或钱聚拢起来。

entries.definition: To care for someone while they grow.
entries.definitionCN: 在某人成长过程中给予照料。

normalIntro.en: The word always needs an object: someone raises something, whether a hand, a price, money, a child, a question or a fear.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词总要带宾语：某人把某样东西举起，无论是手、价格、钱款、孩子、问题还是恐惧。

normal.en: Raise needs an object and rise does not: you raise your hand, but the sun rises.
normal.cn: raise 需要宾语而 rise 不需要：你举起手，而太阳自己升起。

normal.en: A pay raise in American English is what British English calls a pay rise.
normal.cn: 美式英语的 a pay raise 就是英式英语的 a pay rise。

normal.en: Raise money means collect it, while raise prices means increase them: the same verb, two directions of lift.
normal.cn: raise money 是筹集，raise prices 是提高：同一个动词，两种「抬升」方向。

normal.en: Raise children and raise animals both mean care for them until grown.
normal.cn: raise children 与 raise animals 都指照料其长大。

normal.en: Raise a question is to bring it up, not to answer it.
normal.cn: raise a question 是把问题提出来，而不是回答它。

abstract.en: Almost everything people do to improve a situation can be said with this one verb, which is why it appears so often in meetings.
abstract.cn: 人们为改善处境所做的几乎每件事都能用这一个动词表达，所以它在会议里出现得如此频繁。

abstract.en: To raise a child is to lift someone you cannot fully control, and that is the daily risk of parenting.
abstract.cn: 抚养孩子就是托举一个你无法完全掌控的人，这正是养育的日常风险。

abstract.en: A question raised is a question someone must now carry, even if nobody answers it.
abstract.cn: 一个被提出的问题，就成了某人必须背负的问题，即使没有人回答。

examples.en: He raised the box above his head and held it there.
examples.cn: 他把箱子举过头顶，稳稳停在那里。

examples.en: The government plans to raise the minimum wage next year.
examples.cn: 政府计划明年提高最低工资。

examples.en: They raised enough money to rebuild the bridge.
examples.cn: 他们筹到了足够的钱重建那座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞兹」——把东西锐利地向上托起，记住 raise 是举起、提高。

root: 古诺斯语 reisa（举起、立起）→ 中古英语 raise → 现代英语 raise；与 rise、arise 同族。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an upward lift; the senses divide into lifting an object, raising a number, collecting money, bringing up the young, putting a subject forward and causing a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「向上托举」；义项分为举起实物、提高数字、筹集钱款、养育幼小、提出话题与引起情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifted into the air, palm forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举到半空、掌心朝前的手。

branches.en: a box held above the head
branches.cn: 举过头顶的一只箱子

branches.en: a price tag rewritten higher
branches.cn: 被改写成更高数字的价签

branches.en: coins gathered from many hands
branches.cn: 从许多只手里聚拢的硬币

branches.en: a child guided step by step
branches.cn: 一步步被引导的孩子

branches.en: the same lift applied to a question and to a fear
branches.cn: 同一种抬升，一次用于问题，一次用于恐惧

intro.en: The word is a Norse borrowing, and English built its relatives with an agent suffix and a participle rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是古诺斯语借词，英语用施动者词尾与分词来构成亲属词，而非拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 随机的；随意的；无目的的；无规律的；偶然的；随机存取；随机数；胡乱地
definition_en: happening or chosen without a plan, purpose, or pattern, so that no one can predict which one comes next
core_image: 一匹脱缰的马不辨方向地狂奔，马蹄落处扬起的尘土没有一条直线，谁也不知道它下一步踩向哪里
scene: 这里指「随机的」。 A programmer rolls a die across the desk and says: We pick the sample at random, so no single case can skew the result.
sceneCN: 这里 random 先出现在 at random「随机地、胡乱地」（第 2 个义项：16 世纪短语“以极大的速度”引申为“不择方向”），再作「随机抽样的」（第 4 个义项）；句意：我们随机抽取样本，这样任何单个案例都无法让结果偏斜。画面里有骰子、屏幕上的数据表和一支笔。

pos.zh: 随机的；随意的；无规律的；偶然的
（计算机）随机；随意挑选的东西

collocations.zh: 随机选取；随便挑出的组合

derivatives.zh: 随机地；任意地
随机性；无序
使随机化；随机排列
随机化
随机生成器；随机分配器

senses.title: No aim, no target
senses.titleCN: 无目的的：箭射出去，不瞄准任何靶子
senses.definition: made or done without a definite aim, purpose, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 没有明确目标、目的或计划而做出或进行的
senses.example: He made a random guess and happened to be right.
senses.exampleCN: 他随便猜了一下，碰巧猜对了。
senses.why: The adjective is first recorded in the 1650s as 'having no definite aim or purpose, haphazard, not sent in a special direction'. It borrows the image of a rider who has stopped steering.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最早记录于 17 世纪 50 年代，意为“没有确定目标或目的、偶然、未被送往特定方向”。它借用了骑手放开缰绳的意象。

senses.title: At random: at full gallop
senses.titleCN: 胡乱地：原意是“以极大的速度”
senses.definition: in a way that has no plan or order, as in the phrase at random
senses.definitionCN: 毫无计划或秩序地，如短语 at random
senses.example: Books were piled at random on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 书胡乱地堆在地板上。
senses.why: The phrase at random is from the 1560s and first meant 'at great speed', from the old noun randon 'impetuosity, speed'. A horse running full tilt goes wherever momentum takes it, and speed turned into carelessness.
senses.whyCN: 短语 at random 始于 16 世纪 60 年代，原意是“以极大的速度”，来自古名词 randon“冲势、猛劲”。一匹全速奔跑的马跑到哪里全凭惯性，速度就变成了漫不经心。

senses.title: Random access: jump anywhere
senses.titleCN: 随机存取：不必从头读到尾
senses.definition: a way of reading computer memory in which any location can be reached directly, without passing through the ones before it
senses.definitionCN: 一种读取计算机存储器的方式，可直接到达任一位置，无需先经过前面的位置
senses.example: RAM stands for random access memory.
senses.exampleCN: RAM 即随机存取存储器。
senses.why: Random access is recorded from 1953 for memory that need not be read sequentially. Here random does not mean 'by chance' but 'without a fixed order': the head may jump to any address at will.
senses.whyCN: random access 记录于 1953 年，指无需顺序读取的存储器。这里 random 不是“碰运气”，而是“没有固定次序”：磁头可以随意跳到任一地址。

senses.title: Random sample: every case has a chance
senses.titleCN: 随机抽样：每个个体都有同等机会被抽中
senses.definition: a group chosen so that every member of a population has an equal chance of being selected
senses.definitionCN: 这样选出的一组样本：总体中每个成员被选中的机会相等
senses.example: Researchers took a random sample of 500 households.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者随机抽取了 500 户家庭作为样本。
senses.why: Statistics needs a procedure in which no case is favoured. The word's old sense of 'not directed toward a particular target' becomes a technical guarantee: nobody's hand steers the selection.
senses.whyCN: 统计学需要一种不偏袒任何个体的程序。这个词“不被送往特定目标”的旧义变成一项技术保证：没有哪只手在引导选择。

senses.title: No pattern at all
senses.titleCN: 无规律的：看不出可复现的花样
senses.definition: lacking any recognizable pattern, order, or regular arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏可辨认的图案、次序或规则排列的
senses.example: The cracks formed a random pattern across the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 裂缝在墙上形成毫无规律的图案。
senses.why: Once 'no aim' is applied to shapes rather than actions, random means 'no pattern'. The mind looks for a rule and finds none, which is exactly what the word reports.
senses.whyCN: 一旦“无目的”从动作转用到形状，random 就表示“无规律”。头脑去找规则却找不到，这正是这个词所报告的状态。

senses.title: By chance encounter
senses.titleCN: 偶然的：两条路线碰巧交叉
senses.definition: happening by chance rather than by arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 出于偶然而非事先安排而发生的
senses.example: A random meeting in the airport changed her career.
senses.exampleCN: 机场里的一次偶然相遇改变了她的职业道路。
senses.why: The 1650s sense already contained 'haphazard'. Two independent courses crossing without a plan is the everyday picture of chance, so random slides from 'unaimed' to 'unplanned'.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 50 年代的义项已含“偶然”。两条互不相干的路线在没有计划的情况下交叉，正是偶然的日常画面，于是 random 从“无瞄准”滑向“无安排”。

senses.title: That random person
senses.titleCN: 不相干的：不知从哪儿冒出来的那个人
senses.definition: not known or not connected to the people involved; arbitrary or irrelevant, in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 不认识或与当事人无关的；任意、不相干的（非正式用法）
senses.example: Some random guy kept texting her all night.
senses.exampleCN: 一个不知从哪儿冒出来的家伙整晚给她发消息。
senses.why: Colloquial English extended 'no connection' to people: a random stranger is one with no link to your life. The 1980s college slang sense 'person who does not belong on our floor' pushed the word toward 'outsider'.
senses.whyCN: 口语英语把“没有关联”扩展到人：a random stranger 就是与你生活毫无联系的人。20 世纪 80 年代的大学俚语义“不属于我们这层楼的人”，把这个词推向“局外人”。

senses.title: Random numbers, random choices
senses.titleCN: 随机数与随机化：把偶然做成工具
senses.definition: a number or selection produced by a process that has no predictable order, used in computing and research
senses.definitionCN: 由无可预测次序的过程产生的数字或选择，用于计算与研究
senses.example: The app generates a random number between one and ten.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用生成一到十之间的随机数。
senses.why: To use chance, people built machines and algorithms that imitate it: random number, randomize, randomizer. The adjective becomes a noun modifier for the output of an artificial process.
senses.whyCN: 为了利用偶然，人们造出模仿偶然的机器与算法：random number、randomize、randomizer。这个形容词变成名词修饰语，指一个人工过程的产物。

senses.title: Random: the odd one out
senses.titleCN: 俚语里的“怪人”：不属于这里的那一个
senses.definition: in 1980s U.S. college slang, an inferior or undesirable person, especially one who does not belong
senses.definitionCN: 20 世纪 80 年代美国大学俚语中指次等或不受欢迎的人，尤指不属于此处的人
senses.example: Don't bring a random to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 别把不相干的怪人带到派对上。
senses.why: By the 1980s U.S. campus slang had turned the adjective into a noun of contempt for someone outside the group. The 'no connection' sense hardened into social exclusion.
senses.whyCN: 到 20 世纪 80 年代，美国校园俚语把这个形容词变成指称群体之外者的轻蔑名词。“没有关联”的义项硬化成了社会排斥。

intro.en: Random begins as a word for speed: a horse at full gallop has no aim. 'At great speed' became 'carelessly', then 'without plan', and finally the technical 'without fixed order' of computing.
intro.cn: random 起初是一个表示速度的词：全速奔驰的马没有目标。“极快”变成“漫不经心”，再变成“没有计划”，最后成为计算机术语里“没有固定次序”。

items.en: Frankish *rant 'a running' and Proto-Germanic *randa are reconstructed from the Old French and Germanic verbs for running. No written form survives, so this layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 法兰克语 *rant“奔跑”与原始日耳曼语 *randa 是从古法语及日耳曼语各语言的“跑”动词重构出来的。没有书面形式留存，因此这一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Randon meant 'rush, disorder, force, impetuosity', and randir 'to run fast'. The word pictures a charge rather than a stroll.
items.cn: randon 意为“冲势、混乱、力量、猛劲”，randir 意为“快跑”。这个词画的是冲锋，而不是散步。

items.en: The noun randon, randoun is recorded meaning 'impetuosity, speed'. The -n to -m spelling shift parallels seldom and ransom.
items.cn: 名词 randon、randoun 记录于约 1300 年，意为“冲势、速度”。-n 变 -m 的拼写变化与 seldom、ransom 平行。

items.en: The phrase at random appears, first meaning 'at great speed', hence 'carelessly, haphazardly'. Speed and lack of aim are fused in one idiom.
items.cn: 短语 at random 出现，最初意为“以极大的速度”，因此引申为“漫不经心、胡乱地”。速度与无目标在一个习语里熔合了。

items.en: The adjective random is recorded, 'having no definite aim or purpose, haphazard, not sent in a special direction'. The modern statistical sense grows out of this.
items.cn: 形容词 random 被记录，意为“没有确定目标或目的、偶然、未被送往特定方向”。现代统计学义即由此生长出来。

items.en: Random access is recorded in 1953 for computer memory that need not be read sequentially. By the 1980s college slang had added 'inferior, undesirable, out of place'.
items.cn: random access 记录于 1953 年，指无需顺序读取的计算机存储器。到 20 世纪 80 年代，大学俚语又添上“次等的、不受欢迎的、格格不入的”一义。

note.en: The first group shares the ran-/rand- sound and, in two cases, the actual etymology; the second group shares the idea of choosing without a rule.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ran-/rand- 的读音，其中两个词还真有词源关系；第二组共享“不按规则地选择”这一观念。

entries.definition: money paid to free a captive. It is unrelated in meaning but shares the odd -m spelling change with random.
entries.definitionCN: 赎金。意义无关，但与 random 共享那个奇特的 -n 变 -m 拼写变化。

entries.definition: the Middle English noun for 'rush, impetuosity' from which at random was shortened.
entries.definitionCN: 中古英语名词，意为“冲势、猛劲”，at random 即由它缩来。

entries.definition: a unit of currency, or a random value in computing. It looks like a clipped random but is a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: 货币单位，或计算中的随机值。它看起来像 random 的缩写，其实是另一个词。

entries.definition: in a random manner. The adverb looks like the adjective with a tail.
entries.definitionCN: 随机地。这个副词看起来就像形容词多了一条尾巴。

entries.definition: decided by personal choice or impulse rather than reason. It stresses the chooser's freedom, while random stresses the absence of pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 任意的；专断的。它强调选择者的自由，而 random 强调图案的缺失。

entries.definition: with no plan or order, happening as it may. It is close to random but more judgemental.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然的；杂乱的。它接近 random，但更带贬义。

entries.definition: an event that happens without design. It names the cause, while random names the lack of pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然；机会。它命名原因，而 random 命名缺乏规律。

entries.definition: done without care or intention. It suits a casual remark, not a random sample.
entries.definitionCN: 随便的；漫不经心的。它适合一句随口的话，不适合随机样本。

entries.definition: done without choosing carefully, affecting everyone or everything alike.
entries.definitionCN: 不加区别的；滥施的。

normalIntro.en: The real links are speed and horses: Old French randon 'rush', the phrase at random, and ransom's matching -m spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的联想是速度与马：古法语 randon“冲势”、短语 at random，以及 ransom 那同样的 -m 拼写。

normal.en: random and randon: the old noun meant 'rush, impetuosity', so at random first meant 'at full speed'.
normal.cn: random 与 randon：这个古名词意为“冲势、猛劲”，所以 at random 最初意为“全速地”。

normal.en: Think of a horse with no rider: it runs fast and goes nowhere in particular.
normal.cn: 想象一匹没有骑手的马：跑得飞快，却哪里也不去。

normal.en: random access memory does not read in order; it jumps, like a shopper who knows every aisle.
normal.cn: 随机存取存储器不按顺序读；它直接跳，像一个熟悉每条货架的购物者。

normal.en: Random and ransom share the -m: both changed from -n, and neither tells you why.
normal.cn: random 与 ransom 共享那个 -m：两者都由 -n 变来，谁也说不出原因。

normal.en: A random sample is chance made fair: everyone gets the same lottery ticket.
normal.cn: 随机样本是把偶然变得公平：每个人都拿到同样的彩票。

abstract.en: The core is released control: no hand on the reins, no target in sight.
abstract.cn: 核心是放开的控制：缰绳上没有手，视野里没有靶。

abstract.en: Speed, chance, pattern, order: random denies a different thing in each field.
abstract.cn: 速度、偶然、图案、次序：random 在每个领域否认的东西都不一样。

abstract.en: A statistical word built from a galloping horse is the best proof that metaphor becomes method.
abstract.cn: 一个由奔马构成的统计词，正是“隐喻变成方法”的最好证据。

examples.en: The names were chosen at random from a hat.
examples.cn: 名字是从帽子里随机抽出来的。

examples.en: A random error in the data can ruin the whole model.
examples.cn: 数据中的一个随机误差就能毁掉整个模型。

examples.en: She met a random stranger who turned out to be her new boss.
examples.cn: 她偶然遇到一个陌生人，结果竟是她的新上司。

dict_mnemonic.text: ran（跑）+ dom（= dumb 哑的）—— 一匹又跑又哑的马，没有方向地乱冲 → random 随机的；胡乱的

root: 源自古法语 randon“冲势、猛劲”、randir“快跑”，上溯法兰克语 *rant 与原始日耳曼语 *randa“奔跑”，与 run 同族；核心是“一匹全速奔跑却不辨方向的马”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one horse: it gallops without a target, so nothing is aimed, nothing repeats, nothing is in order — and in computing the same word means 'without a fixed sequence'.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一匹马：它没有目标地狂奔，于是没有瞄准、没有重复、没有次序；在计算机里，同一个词就表示“没有固定顺序”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horse galloping with no rider and no destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：一匹没有骑手、也没有目的地的奔马。

branches.en: THE GALLOP: the old phrase 'at speed' and the chance encounter it became.
branches.cn: 奔驰：古老的“全速”短语，以及由此变成的偶然相遇。

branches.en: NO TARGET, NO PATTERN: unaimed action and irregular shape.
branches.cn: 无靶、无纹：没有瞄准的动作，与没有规律的形状。

branches.en: NO FIXED ORDER: memory that jumps, and numbers made by an imitation of chance.
branches.cn: 无固定次序：会跳的存储器，以及模仿偶然造出的数字。

branches.en: FAIR CHANCE: the sample in which every case has the same ticket.
branches.cn: 公平的偶然：每个个体都拿到同样一张票的样本。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDER: the stranger with no link, and the slang name for someone who does not belong.
branches.cn: 局外人：毫无联系的陌生人，以及指称“不属于这里的人”的俚语。

intro.en: Random has no living prefix or suffix in English; it is a whole French noun that became an adjective. Its family shows -ly, -ness, -ize, -ization and the compound random-access.
intro.cn: random 在英语里没有活的前缀或后缀；它是一个整体借来的法语名词，后来变成形容词。它的词族展示 -ly、-ness、-ize、-ization 以及复合词 random-access。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor: the line runs from Frankish *rant through Old French randon and randir to English. Latin is absent from this word's family tree.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁祖先：这条线从法兰克语 *rant 经古法语 randon、randir 到英语。这个词的家谱里没有拉丁语。

items.structure: Old French randon (rush) + English adjective use
items.example: The survey used a random sample of readers.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查使用了随机读者样本。

items.example: The files were randomly assigned to each group.
items.exampleCN: 文件被随机分配给每一组。

items.meaning: the quality of having no pattern
items.example: True randomness is hard to produce by machine.
items.exampleCN: 真正的随机性很难由机器产生。

items.meaning: to arrange in a random order
items.example: The software randomizes the order of the questions.
items.exampleCN: 这个软件会随机打乱题目的顺序。

items.meaning: the act of making something random
items.example: Randomization reduces bias in clinical trials.
items.exampleCN: 随机化可减少临床试验中的偏倚。

items.meaning: a device or program that produces random choices
items.example: The teacher used an online randomizer to call on students.
items.exampleCN: 老师用在线随机器点名。

items.meaning: direct reading of any memory location
items.example: Solid-state drives offer fast random access.
items.exampleCN: 固态硬盘提供快速的随机存取。

items.meaning: a number with no predictable order
items.example: The password generator starts with a random number.
items.exampleCN: 密码生成器以一个随机数开始。

items.example: She opened the book at random and began to read.
items.exampleCN: 她随手翻开书，开始读起来。

definition_zh: 范围；幅度；射程；山脉；在…范围内变动；靶场
definition_en: a set of different things of the same type; the limits within which something varies; the distance a weapon or signal can reach; a line of connected mountains; to vary between two limits; a place for shooting practice
core_image: 一把拉伸开的软尺，刻度从这头排到那头
scene: 清晨的靶场里，射手把标尺架好，远处的山脊像一条长线铺到天边。The rifle had a range of nearly a thousand metres.
sceneCN: 这里 range 是「射程」（第 3 个义项：武器能打到的距离）；句意为这支步枪的射程接近一千米。画面里可留意：架起的标尺、远处的山脊、靶场尽头的靶子。

pos.zh: 范围；幅度；射程；山脉；靶场
在…范围内变动；排列

derivatives.zh: range 加前缀 a-，指按次序摆放、安排
arrange 加 -ment，指排列方式或安排
range 加 -er，指在荒野巡逻的人
range 加 -y，指身形修长、四肢舒展的

senses.title: A set of varieties
senses.definition: a set of different things of the same type, or the limits within which something varies
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物的一个系列，或某物变动的限度
senses.example: The shop sells a wide range of teas.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售种类繁多的茶。
senses.why: From a row of things laid out in order came the idea of a whole series of varieties under one name.
senses.whyCN: 从「按次序排开的一行」生出「同类事物构成的一整个系列」这一概念。

senses.title: A line of mountains
senses.definition: a series of connected hills or mountains forming a long line
senses.definitionCN: 连成一条长线的一串丘陵或山峰
senses.example: A mountain range runs along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 一条山脉沿着边境延伸。
senses.why: Mountains seen from a distance stand in a long row, so the row word was applied to them directly.
senses.whyCN: 远望群山时它们排成长长一行，于是这个「行」的词被直接用在山上。

senses.title: The distance a weapon reaches
senses.definition: the distance over which a gun, missile or signal can reach its target
senses.definitionCN: 枪、导弹或信号能够到达目标的距离
senses.example: The rifle had a range of nearly a thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这支步枪的射程接近一千米。
senses.why: Gunners measured how far a shot could travel, and that measured extent was called its range.
senses.whyCN: 炮手会测量一发炮弹能飞多远，这段被测出的距离就称作它的 range。

senses.title: To vary between limits
senses.definition: to vary between two fixed limits, used of prices, sizes, temperatures and the like
senses.definitionCN: 在两个固定限度之间变动，用于价格、尺寸、温度等
senses.example: Temperatures range from ten to thirty degrees here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的气温在十到三十度之间变动。
senses.why: Once range named the limits themselves, the verb could describe anything moving between them.
senses.whyCN: range 一旦指限度本身，动词便可用来说明任何在限度之间移动的事物。

senses.title: A place for shooting practice
senses.definition: an area laid out with targets where people practise shooting
senses.definitionCN: 排布着靶子、供人练习射击的场地
senses.example: The recruits spent the morning at the shooting range.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵们在射击场度过了一个上午。
senses.why: A range is also a measured stretch of ground, and a shooting ground is exactly that: a marked extent with targets.
senses.whyCN: range 也指一段测好的地面，而射击场正是如此：一片标好的、设有靶子的场地。

intro.en: Range comes from Old French range, a row or line, probably from a Frankish word for a ring of men; all its senses grew from the idea of things set out in order.
intro.cn: range 来自古法语 range（一行、一列），可能源自法兰克语中表示一圈人的词；所有义项都从「按次序排开」这一想法生长出来。

items.en: Old French range meant a row or line, and it named things placed in order.
items.cn: 古法语 range 意为一行或一列，用来命名按次序摆放的东西。

items.en: The word is traced to a Frankish term for a ring or band of men, which gave the idea of a line.
items.cn: 这个词可追溯到法兰克语中表示一圈或一队人的词，由此产生「一行」的概念。

items.en: Middle English used range for a row and a rank, and then for the extent something could cover.
items.cn: 中古英语用 range 指一排、一列，随后又指某物所能覆盖的范围。

items.en: Gunners spoke of the range of a shot, and the word became the measured distance a weapon could reach.
items.cn: 炮手们会说一发炮弹的 range，这个词便成了武器能到达的实测距离。

items.en: Modern English extends range to mountains, to variation between limits, and to grounds for shooting practice.
items.cn: 现代英语把 range 扩展到山脉、限度之间的变动，以及练习射击的场地。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same row-and-line idea; the near-meaning group gathers words for extent and distance.
note.cn: 形近组收基于同一「排列成行」概念构成的词；近义组收表示范围与距离的词。

entries.definition: To put things in a particular order.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物按特定次序摆放。

entries.definition: The way things are put in order.
entries.definitionCN: 事物摆放的方式。

entries.definition: A person who patrols and protects a wild area.
entries.definitionCN: 巡逻并保护荒野的人。

entries.definition: A row or a position in order, a related Germanic word.
entries.definitionCN: 一行或在次序中的位置，相关的日耳曼词。

entries.definition: The area or degree that something covers.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所覆盖的面积或程度。

entries.definition: The range of what something deals with.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所涉及的范围。

entries.definition: The distance or time from one end to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 从一端到另一端的距离或时间。

entries.definition: The space between two points.
entries.definitionCN: 两点之间的空间。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a row, then widens into a series, a reachable distance, a line of hills, a spread of values and a marked ground.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一行开始，逐步扩展为系列、可达的距离、连绵的山、数值的跨度，以及标好的场地。

normal.en: Range and arrange share the same old row, one naming the line and the other the act of setting it out.
normal.cn: range 与 arrange 共享同一个古老的「行」，一个命名这条线，一个命名把线排开的行为。

normal.en: A mountain range is simply mountains standing in a long row.
normal.cn: 一条 mountain range 就是排成长长一行的山。

normal.en: A rifle's range is how far its shot can travel before it falls.
normal.cn: 步枪的 range 是子弹在落下之前能飞多远。

normal.en: When prices range from low to high, they vary between two limits.
normal.cn: 当价格 range from low to high，它们就在两个限度之间变动。

normal.en: A shooting range is a field laid out with targets for practice.
normal.cn: shooting range 是排好靶子供练习的场地。

abstract.en: Range names the space between a starting point and a limit, whether in distance, price or ability.
abstract.cn: range 是「起点与限度之间的空间」这个词，无论那空间在距离、价格还是能力上。

abstract.en: To say something is out of range is to say it lies beyond where your reach stops.
abstract.cn: 说某物 out of range，就是说它落在你触及范围的边界之外。

abstract.en: A wide range is not just many things but many things set side by side in order.
abstract.cn: a wide range 不只是许多东西，而是许多东西按次序并排摆开。

examples.en: The shop sells a wide range of teas.
examples.cn: 这家店出售种类繁多的茶。

examples.en: The missile has a range of over two thousand kilometres.
examples.cn: 这种导弹的射程超过两千公里。

examples.en: Temperatures range from ten to thirty degrees here.
examples.cn: 这里的气温在十到三十度之间变动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「软尺」——把软尺拉开来量，从这头到那头都是范围，记住 range 是范围、射程、山脉。

root: 古法语 range（一行、一列）→ 中古英语 range → 现代英语 range；可能与法兰克语「一圈人」有关。同族有 arrange、arrangement、ranger。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a row laid out in order; the senses move from a series of varieties to a line of mountains, the reach of a weapon, variation between limits and a shooting ground.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是按次序排开的一行；义项从同类系列，到山脉，再到武器可达的距离、限度之间的变动，以及射击场地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft measuring tape stretched out, its marks running in a straight row.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把拉伸开的软尺，刻度排成笔直的一行。

branches.en: a shelf of bottles lined up in a row
branches.cn: 一排摆开的瓶子

branches.en: ridges running to the horizon
branches.cn: 延伸至地平线的山脊

branches.en: a marked distance on a rifle sight
branches.cn: 步枪准星上标出的距离

branches.en: a thermometer rising and falling
branches.cn: 上下浮动的温度计

branches.en: targets standing at the far end of a field
branches.cn: 立在场地尽头的靶子

intro.en: The word is a borrowing from Old French, and its family is built with English prefixes, suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词借自古法语，其词族由英语前缀、后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word; the older root is Frankish.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录；更早的词根是法兰克语。

definition_zh: 等级；地位；军衔；行列；把…分等级；位居
definition_en: a position on a scale of importance or quality; an official grade, especially in the armed forces; a row of people or things; to place people or things in order; to hold a particular position
core_image: 一排士兵按高矮站成的笔直队列
scene: 操场上，士兵们按个头从高到矮站成一条直线，队伍整齐得像尺子画出来。The captain held the rank of major for many years.
sceneCN: 这里 rank 是「军衔」（第 2 个义项：军队中的正式等级）；句意为这位上尉多年保持少校军衔。画面里可留意：整齐的队伍、按身高排成的直线、军装的肩章。

pos.zh: 等级；地位；军衔；行列
把…分等级；排列；位居

derivatives.zh: rank 加 -ing，指名次、排名
rank 加 -ed，指被排定名次的
out- 与 rank 复合，指地位高于
high 与 ranking 复合，指级别高的

senses.title: A position on a scale
senses.definition: a position on a scale of importance, quality or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 在重要性、质量或成就的尺度上所居的位置
senses.example: She reached the top rank of her profession.
senses.exampleCN: 她达到了本行业的最高等级。
senses.why: A row of soldiers fixes each person in a place, and that fixed place became a measure of standing.
senses.whyCN: 一排士兵把每个人固定在某个位置，这个固定位置便成了地位的衡量。

senses.title: An official grade
senses.definition: an official grade held by a member of the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 武装部队成员所持的正式等级
senses.example: The captain held the rank of major.
senses.exampleCN: 这位上尉持有少校军衔。
senses.why: Armies number their rows from bottom to top, so the place a soldier occupies became his official grade.
senses.whyCN: 军队把队列自下而上编号，因此士兵所占的位置便成了他的正式等级。

senses.title: A row of people or things
senses.definition: a row of people or things placed side by side
senses.definitionCN: 并排而立的一排人或物
senses.example: The chairs stood in a neat rank along the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 椅子沿墙排成整齐的一行。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a row, the line in which people or objects are drawn up.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是一排，即人或物被排成的直线。

senses.title: To place in order
senses.definition: to arrange people or things in order according to quality or importance
senses.definitionCN: 按质量或重要性把人或物排成次序
senses.example: The judges ranked the entries from best to worst.
senses.exampleCN: 评委把参赛作品从优到劣排出名次。
senses.why: If a rank is a row, to rank is to put things into that row in their proper places.
senses.whyCN: 既然 rank 是一行，to rank 就是把事物各归其位地排进那一行。

senses.title: To hold a position
senses.definition: to have a particular position in a scale, list or group
senses.definitionCN: 在尺度、名单或群体中占据特定位置
senses.example: The university ranks among the best in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学位居全国最好的大学之列。
senses.why: From the act of placing came the state of being placed, so a thing can rank, that is, stand somewhere in the order.
senses.whyCN: 从「摆放」的动作生出「被摆放」的状态，因此某物可以 rank，即在次序中站于某处。

intro.en: Rank comes from Old French ranc, a row, probably from the same Frankish source as range; a row of soldiers became a scale of official grades.
intro.cn: rank 来自古法语 ranc（一行），可能与 range 同出法兰克语；一排士兵后来变成了等级阶梯。

items.en: Old French ranc meant a row or line, especially a row of soldiers.
items.cn: 古法语 ranc 意为一行或一列，尤指一排士兵。

items.en: The word is traced to a Frankish term for a circle or band of men, the same source as range.
items.cn: 这个词可追溯到法兰克语中表示一圈或一队人的词，与 range 同源。

items.en: Middle English rank kept both the row and the military line, and added the idea of a grade.
items.cn: 中古英语 rank 既保留「一排」与军阵的线，又加上了等级的意思。

items.en: Because a formation places each soldier in a fixed spot, rank came to mean a soldier's official grade.
items.cn: 由于队列把每个士兵放在固定位置，rank 便引申为士兵的正式等级。

items.en: Modern English ranks people and things by quality, and uses the verb to rank for placing and for holding a place.
items.cn: 现代英语按质量给人或物排等级，并用动词 rank 表示排位和位居。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers row words and close forms; the near-meaning group gathers words for grade and standing.
note.cn: 形近组收表示行列的词与近形词；近义组收表示等级与地位的词。

entries.definition: A row or extent, the close cousin of rank.
entries.definitionCN: 一行或范围，rank 的近亲。

entries.definition: A position on a list of results.
entries.definitionCN: 成绩榜单上的名次。

entries.definition: Placed in order by grade.
entries.definitionCN: 按等级排好的。

entries.definition: A person who patrols a wild area.
entries.definitionCN: 巡逻荒野的人。

entries.definition: A level of quality or rank.
entries.definitionCN: 质量或等级的层次。

entries.definition: A person's social or official standing.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的社会地位或官方身份。

entries.definition: A place in a scale or order.
entries.definitionCN: 在尺度或次序中的位置。

entries.definition: A division based on quality or rank.
entries.definitionCN: 按质量或等级划分的类别。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a row of bodies, then becomes the place each body occupies, and finally the act and state of standing somewhere in an order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一排身体开始，变成每具身体所占的位置，最后成为「处于某个次序位置」的动作与状态。

normal.en: Rank and range come from the same old word for a row.
normal.cn: rank 与 range 同出表示「一行」的那个古词。

normal.en: A rank of soldiers is a row; an officer's rank is his place in that row.
normal.cn: 士兵的 rank 是一排；军官的 rank 是他在这一排里的位置。

normal.en: To rank first is to stand at the head of the row.
normal.cn: to rank first 就是站在这支队伍的最前头。

normal.en: Rank and file names the ordinary soldiers who stand in the rows.
normal.cn: rank and file 指站在队列里的普通士兵。

normal.en: To rank something is to put it into its proper place in the line.
normal.cn: 给某物 rank 就是把它放到队列中合适的位置。

abstract.en: Rank measures where you stand, not who you are.
abstract.cn: rank 衡量的是你站在哪里，而不是你是谁。

abstract.en: A list ranks names the way a formation ranks bodies, by a fixed order.
abstract.cn: 名单给名字排名，正如队列给身体排名，都依一种固定次序。

abstract.en: To outrank someone is to stand one step nearer the front.
abstract.cn: outrank 某人，就是比他站得离排头更近一步。

examples.en: He rose to the rank of colonel.
examples.cn: 他升到了上校军衔。

examples.en: The university ranks among the best in the country.
examples.cn: 这所大学位居全国最好的大学之列。

examples.en: The students were ranked by their test scores.
